blockedReason: Only 7 of 13 hooks are recovered, so this profile is NOT usable for a release. The four skin NoteMove hooks are confirmed by two independent signals (instruction-skeleton similarity 81-85%, and a unique BL caller at exactly the same distance as the audited 157 build: 9948 / 8564 / 8424 / 6040 bytes). The judgment hooks (click, drag, flick, hold, result, miss) are unresolved: their 157 prologues are 4-5 instruction stubs that are nearly identical across all four control classes, and unlike the skin hooks they have between 3 and 11 BL callers, so the caller-distance fingerprint is not unique and the skeleton match cannot separate them. Resolving them needs either a device-side trace or manual disassembly with named field cross-references.

recoveryNotes.method: instruction-skeleton (48 instructions, address immediates masked) + caller-distance fingerprint, bijective assignment
recoveryNotes.selfCheck: recover_profile.py recovers 13/13 hooks with byte-identical RVAs when the target is the 157 reference itself

recoveryNotes.rejectedApproach: il2cpp metadata method-record table: on 4.1.0 it resolves NoteMove to 0x1d7efc4, which is 22236 bytes away from the address confirmed by skeleton + caller distance (0x1d846a0). That table is therefore not the method table this build's hooks need.
